## Requirement
WHEN a finding's handler is mounted under more than one route tier (`/public`, `/external`, `/internal` = one tier group, TIERS
in correlate.py card_twins) and the twin is proved by TASK-160 (same phase 0 card, >=1 shared handler ref), the engine SHALL show
every mount next to the finding, e.g. `Endpoint: POST /external/v1/books/recommend; also mounted: POST /internal/v1/books/recommend
(same handler, card refs app/routers/books.py:25)`, in the phase 1 report rows, graph/correlation and the 2b item text. The finding
`endpoint` field stays exactly as written (stable ids, tracking, coverage); the extra line is engine-derived from `twins.list`;
exposure is rated by the most exposed mount (public > external > internal) for display only; no prompt change.


## Acceptance
<!-- Each item objectively verifiable. VERIFIED requires every box ticked. -->
- [ ] AC1: finding JSON, results, conclusion.json `endpoint` and stable ids unchanged (byte diff of findings; track.sh adds 0 ids).
- [ ] AC2: a finding with a proved twin shows "also mounted: <M> <route> (same handler, card refs ...)" in the phase 1 / security report row, by-repo, exec notes and the graph node; a finding without one renders byte-identical.
- [ ] AC3: the 2b item for a twin lists both routes (already `via_twin`); the 2b report row shows the same "also mounted" line.
- [ ] AC4: one tier group public/external/internal; a mount under no tier prefix gets no twin (no guess).
- [ ] AC5: report_qa PASS, coverage_check gaps=0, single-source plans byte-identical (no phase 0 cards).

- [ ] AC6: (RAW-01085, http-v16) an `endpoint` written as `M /external/...; M /internal/...` is accepted as is; the engine derives `Exposure: <tier> (most exposed of <tiers>)` with rank public > external > internal; a v15 finding listing one mount gets the second from a proved TASK-160 twin.

- [ ] AC7: (RAW-01087) logreach never queries an `/internal/` mount on the public WAF host as the finding's own route (Kong does not route it). A finding with only `/internal/` mounts gets its verdict from callers only: caller_link / via_caller when a public caller reaches it (2b chain, correlate R1, mesh note), else a closed "in-cluster only, no public caller found" state, never "not_seen, suggested Low".
- [ ] AC8: (RAW-01087) a multi-mount finding is checked on its public/external mounts; its `/internal/` mount is used for caller matching (correlate R1 and the logreach link) exactly like a TASK-160 twin, with the endpoint itself as the proof.
- [ ] AC9: (RAW-01087) reports show the exposure line and, for internal-only findings, "in-cluster; reached via <caller>" or the in-cluster state; severity, confidence and prerequisites stay as the prompt wrote them (v16: one level lower). Fixtures come from the v16 sample findings.json (security_prompt_qa http-v16-upzi-learning-opus55-pc1).
- [ ] AC10: (RAW-01088) the previous Upzi/full run 20261026-060019 stays on disk; the new run is compared with it (run_diff + tracking stable ids): moved severities and endpoints listed; no finding id lost through the endpoint format change (T3 shared route matches a multi-mount endpoint).
- [ ] AC11: skill api-platform-security carries the v16 "one handler, several mounts" rule (CLAUDE.md: prompt and skill change together).
